Plot Categorical Variable Distribution

Source: R/plt_dist.R
plt_dist.Rd

Visualise the cross-distribution of categorical variables. With 2 variables the plot is an alluvial / Sankey flow (default) or a stacked proportion bar, selected via type; with 3 variables it is a tile heatmap. The alluvial mode uses plt_alluvial(), so it supports native faceting and only requires the suggested ggalluvial package.

Usage

plt_dist(
  data,
  dis_vars,
  type = c("alluvial", "bar"),
  facet = NULL,
  color = NULL,
  alpha = 0.7,
  label_args = list(style = "count_percent", min_pct = 0, size = NULL, color = "black",
    box = TRUE, fill = "white", alpha = 1, pct_accuracy = 0.1),
  flow_args = list(curve_type = "linear"),
  stratum_args = list(width = 0.5, color = "gray50", linewidth = 0.3, gap = 0.01),
  facet_args = list(nrow = NULL, ncol = NULL, scales = "fixed"),
  legend_args = list(position = NULL, ncol = 1),
  theme_use = theme_heat(14),
  save = list()
)

Arguments

data

A data frame. Existing dplyr grouping is ignored; counts use only the variables selected by dis_vars and facet. Rows missing any required value are removed with a message in every mode; unrelated columns do not affect inclusion. An error is raised if no complete rows remain. Alluvial mode also removes explicit NA factor levels and SPSS user-defined missing values. The heatmap ignores facet.

dis_vars

Character vector of 2 or 3 distinct, non-empty column names. Plain integer and double columns are treated as categories in numeric ascending order in every mode; values are not binned. Labelled columns (haven_labelled, also as facet) are converted with labelled::to_factor(), so they show their value labels. Existing factors keep their level order. Character columns retain their existing ordering: first appearance for alluvial plots, sorted for bar charts and heatmaps.

  • 2 variables: c(x, fill) \(\rightarrow\) alluvial flow (type = "alluvial", default) or stacked bar (type = "bar").

  • 3 variables: c(x, y, fill) \(\rightarrow\) tile heatmap (type ignored). Each observed (x, y) cell must have only one fill category; otherwise an error prevents overplotting.

type

Plot type for the 2-variable case: "alluvial" (default) or "bar" (stacked proportion bar on a percentage axis, with the first fill category on top as in the legend and the alluvial plot). Ignored when dis_vars has 3 variables.

facet

Optional faceting variable name (string). Used by both 2-variable plot types and must differ from dis_vars; ignored for the 3-variable heatmap. Plain integer and double facet values use numeric ascending order; existing factors keep their level order. Panel layout follows facet_args.

color

Colour specification, resolved by the internal colour resolver: NULL (default pal_lancet), a registered palette name (e.g. "Paired"), a single literal colour, or a vector of colours. In a named vector, names must be unique category labels and include every observed fill category. Unnamed vectors follow factor-level order (data order for character alluvial groups). Unused bar/heatmap factor levels retain their positions in an unnamed palette.

alpha

One finite number between 0 and 1 giving the opacity of the bar segments and heatmap tiles, and of the flow ribbons in alluvial mode (where plt_alluvial() calls it flow_args$alpha). Default 0.7.

label_args

A named list controlling the in-plot labels:

style

Character scalar selecting label content. Default "count_percent". Bar chart: "count_percent" gives count (percent) on one line, "count_percent_wrap" puts the count above the percentage, "count" and "percent" give one of them, and "none" hides the labels. Alluvial plot: "count_percent" gives name (count, percent), "count_percent_wrap" puts the name above count (percent), "count" gives name (count), "percent" gives name percent, and "none" hides the labels. Heatmap: any value other than "none" prints the third variable's category in each tile; "none" hides the labels and shows the fill legend. Counts use a comma as thousands separator.

min_pct

Numeric scalar in \([0, 1]\). Bar segments and alluvial strata whose within-category proportion is below it are left unlabelled. Not used by the heatmap. Default 0.

size

NULL or a positive number giving the ggplot2 text size. NULL (default) scales with the base font size of theme_use: (base_size - 4) / .pt on bars, (base_size - 2) / .pt on the heatmap and 3 * base_size / 14 in alluvial mode.

color

Character scalar giving the label text colour. Default "black".

box

Logical scalar. TRUE (default) draws boxed labels; FALSE draws plain text.

fill

Character scalar giving the label box background; used only when box = TRUE. Default "white".

alpha

Numeric scalar in \([0, 1]\) giving the label opacity. Default 1.

pct_accuracy

Positive number giving the rounding accuracy of percentages, as in scales::percent(): 0.1 (default) keeps one decimal place and 1 gives whole percentages. Not used by the heatmap.

flow_args

A named list for the flow ribbons, used only in alluvial mode:

curve_type

Character scalar: "linear" (default), "cubic", "quintic", "sine", "arctangent", "sigmoid" or "xspline".

The ribbon opacity is set by alpha.

stratum_args

A named list for the strata, used only in alluvial mode:

width

Number in \((0, 1]\) giving the stratum width relative to the spacing of the x positions. Default 0.5.

color

Character scalar giving the stratum border colour. Default "gray50".

linewidth

Non-negative number giving the stratum border width. Default 0.3.

gap

Non-negative number giving the transparent gap between strata as a fraction of the panel height; the gaps together must stay below 1. Default 0.01; 0 removes them.

facet_args

A named list controlling ggplot2::facet_wrap() when facet is set (bar and alluvial modes):

nrow

NULL or a positive integer giving the number of panel rows. NULL (default) puts up to three panels in a row on bar charts (unless ncol is set) and keeps facet_wrap()'s layout in alluvial mode. Only facet values present in the data are counted.

ncol

NULL or a positive integer giving the number of panel columns. Default NULL.

scales

"fixed" (default), "free", "free_x" or "free_y".

legend_args

A named list controlling the fill legend:

position

NULL or one of "right", "left", "top", "bottom", "none". NULL (default) keeps the automatic placement: the bar chart uses the theme's position, or "right" when the theme hides the legend (as the default theme_heat() does); the heatmap hides the legend when its tiles are labelled and otherwise places it like the bar chart; the alluvial plot uses "right".

ncol

Positive integer giving the number of legend columns. Default 1.

theme_use

Theme specification, resolved by the internal theme resolver. Default theme_heat(14) (clean look). Also accepts a ggplot2::theme object, a theme function, a function-name string (e.g. "theme_my"), or NULL (\(\rightarrow\) theme_km()). Unless label_args$size is set, label sizes follow the theme's base font size, e.g. theme_use = theme_my(base_size = 16). In alluvial mode only the base font size is taken from theme_use; theme_alluvia() supplies the remaining theme settings.

save

NULL, an empty list (default), or a named list forwarded to RegR::save_plt() for PDF output: filename and optionally width and height. A width or height left out defaults to the page the plot is laid out for – for the alluvial plot see plt_alluvial(); 0.9 in per x level (at least 3 in) by 4 in per facet for the bar chart, and 1.1 in per column by 0.6 in per row of cells for the heatmap, beside the measured axis text and legend – which every call prints with the matching save line. Saving, and the size note, need the RegR package.

Value

A ggplot object carrying that page size as attr(p, "plot_size"), c(width, height) in inches.

Details

The list arguments (label_args, flow_args, stratum_args, facet_args, legend_args) follow plt_alluvial(): a partial list is merged with the defaults shown in the usage, and unknown or duplicated fields are rejected.

See also

Other plot: PlotButterfly(), PlotButterfly2(), PlotRankCor(), plt_cat(), plt_con(), plt_sankey(), plt_upset()

Examples

set.seed(1)
df <- data.frame(
  stage = factor(sample(c("I","II","III","IV"), 200, TRUE)),
  sex   = factor(sample(c("M","F"), 200, TRUE)),
  race  = factor(sample(c("White","Black","Asian"), 200, TRUE)),
  grade = factor(sample(c("Low","Mid","High"), 200, TRUE))
)

# --- Stacked bar (type = "bar") -------------------------------------------
# "count (percent)" labels on one line
plt_dist(df, dis_vars = c("stage", "sex"), type = "bar")


# Count above percent, whole percentages, segments below 10% unlabelled
plt_dist(df, dis_vars = c("stage", "sex"), type = "bar",
         label_args = list(style = "count_percent_wrap", pct_accuracy = 1,
                           min_pct = 0.1))


# Percent-only labels, facets in one column, legend below
plt_dist(df, dis_vars = c("stage", "sex"), type = "bar", facet = "race",
         label_args = list(style = "percent"),
         facet_args = list(ncol = 1),
         legend_args = list(position = "bottom", ncol = 2))


# No labels
plt_dist(df, dis_vars = c("stage", "sex"), type = "bar",
         label_args = list(style = "none"))


# Registered palette name / literal colour vector
plt_dist(df, dis_vars = c("stage", "sex"), type = "bar", color = "Paired")

plt_dist(df, dis_vars = c("stage", "sex"), type = "bar",
         color = c("steelblue", "tomato"))


# Theme + label size carried by theme_use
plt_dist(df, dis_vars = c("stage", "sex"), type = "bar",
         theme_use = theme_my(base_size = 16))


# --- Tile heatmap (3 variables; type ignored) -----------------------------
heat_data <- expand.grid(stage = c("I", "II", "III", "IV"),
                         grade = c("Low", "Mid", "High"))
heat_data$category <- factor(rep(c("A", "B"), 6))
plt_dist(heat_data, dis_vars = c("stage", "grade", "category"))

plt_dist(heat_data, dis_vars = c("stage", "grade", "category"),
         label_args = list(style = "none"))


# --- Alluvial flow (default; needs ggalluvial) ----------------------------
if (requireNamespace("ggalluvial", quietly = TRUE)) {
  plt_dist(df, dis_vars = c("stage", "sex"))
  plt_dist(df, dis_vars = c("stage", "sex"), facet = "race")
  plt_dist(df, dis_vars = c("stage", "sex"),
           label_args = list(style = "count_percent_wrap"))
  plt_dist(df, dis_vars = c("stage", "sex"),
           flow_args = list(curve_type = "sigmoid"),
           stratum_args = list(width = 0.4, gap = 0.02))
}
